job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

response.passage: Mr. Sharma stood near the vibrant stalls of the Sunday Farmers Market with his students, Rohan and Meera. 'Look at the variety,' Mr. Sharma said, pointing toward the organic produce. 'The local farmers bring their harvest here every week because the soil in the nearby village of Rampur is rich in minerals.' Rohan noticed a vendor selling honey. 'Sir, why is this jar priced at 150 rupees?' Rohan asked. Mr. Sharma explained, 'The price is higher because the bees are fed exclusively on wild lavender flowers, which are rare.' Meera pointed to a display of apples. 'I read that 400 kilograms of these apples were sold yesterday,' she noted. Mr. Sharma smiled, 'That is correct, Meera. The market has grown significantly since 2012, when it first started with only five stalls.' As they walked, Rohan felt exhausted from the heat. 'I am tired, so the market must be tired too,' he joked. Mr. Sharma laughed, 'The market is a place of trade, not a living being, Rohan. It remains busy because people value fresh food.'
response.summary: Mr. Sharma takes his students, Rohan and Meera, to a local farmers market to observe trade. They discuss the reasons behind produce pricing and the history of the market's growth. The visit highlights the difference between agricultural facts and personal feelings.
